clauses.mechanism: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; 51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) orders that the listed Executive Orders, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:", in a two-column table headed 'No. Subject'; its entry "11431 Creating a board of inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the maritime industry" names this order by number. A scan of the full held text of EO 12553 for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending finds those strings only inside table subjects (the words effectiveness and Suspending), not as operative wording, so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, 1986-02-25; that is an inference from the heading and signature block, not express wording.
clauses.reason: whole: The printed order creates a board of inquiry under section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act, appoints its members, gives it the powers and duties of Title II of the Act, sets a report due by October 2, 1968 (the order's words are "on or before October 2," followed by 1968 on the next line), and provides that the Board continues in existence after reporting. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes it by number ("11431 Creating a board of inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the maritime industry"). The report date is a deadline, not an end, and no held source establishes the Board's actual report or discharge, so no earlier end or later event is recorded. The order states no end date of its own, and the by-number scan of held order texts finds no later order citing it.

inventory_overrides.reason: The dossier's inventory for this order does not cover the whole printed order (it starts after the opening paragraphs or splits the report date from its year). The corrected clause spans the printed order from its heading through its last operative sentence; the order has no numbered sections, so one clause is the complete inventory.

research_rationale:
EO 11431 (signed 1968-09-30; 33 FR 14697 (Federal Register of October 2, 1968; PDF page 7)) creates a board of inquiry under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 to inquire into labor disputes between steamship companies, contracting stevedores, contracting marine carpenters, lighterage operators and other employers in related pier activities at Atlantic and Gulf Coast and other ports and certain of their employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association, which had resulted in a threatened strike, appoints David L. Cole (Chairman), Peter Seitz and Monsignor George G. Higgins, gives the Board the powers and duties of Title II of that Act, directs it to report to the President in accordance with section 206 "on or before October 2," 1968, and provides that upon submission of its report the Board continues in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the Act. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11431.txt); its printed number, title, page and signature date match the census register row. The dossier's clause inventory splits the order mid-sentence or omits its opening paragraphs, so I replaced it with one clause covering the printed order from its heading to its last operative sentence (characters 518-2542); the order has no numbered sections. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25) revokes the order by number in its revocation table, and that express revocation is the first end. The report date is a deadline, not an end; no report of this Board is held (a search of the held texts for the order's number and subject words found none), so no report or discharge date is recorded as a later event. Bounded search: the dossier's three machine searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts); the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).

A report date is a deadline, not an end. No held source establishes when the Board reported, whether the dispute settled, or whether the Board was ever discharged, so no earlier end is claimed. The by-number scan finds no held later order citing this order (its hits are copies of the order itself); EO 12553 names it in the number column of its revocation table, which the regex scan does not match, and I found that entry by reading. savings.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception or pending-matter wording: a scan of its full held text for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending finds those strings only inside table subjects. The revocation therefore leaves no part of this order in operation. The order created no continuing right or fund; whatever the Board did before the revocation is a completed fact whose dates are not established by a held source.
